explain.say: If you went back in time 4.5 billion years, you could not breathe! There was almost no oxygen. Look at the timeline. It starts with young Earth, covered in erupting volcanoes, puffing out steam and carbon dioxide.

explain.say: Less! Look at 3 billion years ago. Tiny ocean life, simple algae and bacteria, began photosynthesis: taking in carbon dioxide and giving out oxygen. Slowly oxygen built up, as you can see at 2.4 billion years ago. What do you think life needed next?

explain.say: Protection from the Sun! See the ozone layer forming? Oxygen high up made ozone, which blocks harmful ultraviolet light, so life could later spread onto land. Carbon got locked away in rocks and fossil fuels. Which gas do you think went down as oxygen went up?

faq.a: As the early Earth cooled, water vapour from volcanoes condensed and fell as rain for millions of years, collecting into oceans. Some water may also have come from icy comets and asteroids.
asks: Where did Earth's water come from?

faq.a: Oxygen came from photosynthesis by algae and bacteria, and later plants. They took in carbon dioxide and released oxygen, slowly building it up over billions of years.
asks: How did oxygen get into the atmosphere?

faq.q: What is the air made of today?
faq.a: Dry air is about 78 percent nitrogen, 21 percent oxygen, almost 1 percent argon, and small amounts of other gases, including about 0.04 percent carbon dioxide.
Carbon dioxide dissolved in the oceans, was used by algae and plants in photosynthesis, and was locked away in sedimentary rocks like limestone and in fossil fuels.
asks: Where did the early carbon dioxide go?

faq.q: What was the Great Oxidation Event?
faq.a: Around 2.4 billion years ago, oxygen from photosynthesis began to build up in the air for the first time. It changed the chemistry of the whole planet.
asks: When did oxygen appear in the air?

facts: Dry air today is about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 0.9% argon and about 0.04% carbon dioxide.
The Great Oxidation Event, when oxygen first built up in the atmosphere, began about 2.4 billion years ago.
